critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal, correct, and addresses the shared root cause (URL-agnostic regex passes) rather than patching the single reported string — good hygiene.

_URL_RE = r'https?://\S+' is greedy on trailing punctuation (period, closing paren, comma) — the URL span captured may include a trailing sentence terminator or the closing ')' of a markdown link. Because the fix restores bytes verbatim, this is functionally harmless (the URL round-trips exactly), but it means the *sentinel* also swallowed the trailing char, so any downstream markdown parser sees the URL exactly as the model emitted it. Not a bug; noting as a subtle characteristic of the regex.

The \x00-delimited sentinel is a clean choice — no collision risk with the map/filename regexes. Consider a brief comment noting why null bytes are safe (they can never appear in LLM-emitted UTF-8 text under normal conditions) for future maintainers.
No regression risk observed in the 37-test pre-existing suite; the change is well-contained to filter_for_business_owner().

Suggestion (non-blocking): a fuzz-style property test that generates random URLs inside random prose could future-proof this filter against any new map entry addition — but the current 9 URL-focused tests already lock the concrete failure modes.

rca of the issue: Root cause (already fixed): filter_for_business_owner() applied _FILENAME_RE, _combined_pattern (word-jargon map), and _ACCESS_TO_RE substitutions across the entire reply string with zero URL-awareness. The word 'github' inside 'github.com' is a whole word by \b boundary standards, so the map entry 'github' -> "website's connection" fired inside URL domains exactly as it would in prose, producing the broken 'https://website\'s connection.com/...'. Same class of bug would fire for any URL whose path ended in a recognized extension (e.g. '.json') via _FILENAME_RE. Reproduction: filter_for_business_owner('Commit: https://github.com/x/y/z') would return 'Commit: https://website\'s connection.com/x/y/z' pre-fix. Mitigation (applied): new _URL_RE = re.compile(r'https?://\S+') extracts every URL into a null-byte-delimited sentinel BEFORE any substitution pass runs, then restores each URL byte-for-byte AFTER all passes complete. This immunizes URLs against any current or future map entry / filename regex.
